blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team needs one rule enforced for every command, with an explanation given to Claude, and the rule must hold in every project that installs their tooling. Which design fits?

options.text: A skill in each repository that tells Claude to avoid the action
options.says: Ruled out because "a skill is instructions Claude may follow", and not a rule that holds.

options.text: A hook in a plugin that blocks with exit code 2 and a reason
options.says: The hooks section gives "deterministic control: certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them", exit 2 blocks and "Write a reason to stderr", and a plugin carries the hook to every project that enables it.

options.text: A subagent in the plugin that reviews each command before it runs
options.says: Ruled out because a subagent is "An isolated context that returns summarised results" and is not a gate for every command.

options.text: A line in each memory file that forbids the action by its name
options.says: Ruled out because a memory file holds "Persistent context loaded every conversation", which is guidance and not enforcement.

questions.stem: One skill drafts release summaries, and another tags and ships a release. Which pair of settings fits?

options.text: Automatic loading off for the first, left on for the second
options.says: Ruled out because a skill that tags a release "has side effects, and a person should start it", and this reversal leaves that skill to Claude.

options.text: Automatic loading left on for both, with `Bash` pre-approved on the second
options.says: Ruled out because "`allowed-tools: Bash` approves every shell command for that turn", and a skill with side effects should not load by itself either.

options.text: Automatic loading off for both, with nothing pre-approved on either
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude loads it by itself when your request matches its description", and the harmless skill gains from that.

options.text: Automatic loading left on for the first, off for the second
options.says: The page says "A skill that writes release notes is harmless and Claude can start it when asked", while a skill with side effects needs `disable-model-invocation: true`.

origin.section: Who starts it and what it may do

questions.stem: A repository's `.claude/settings.json` registers a marketplace and enables a plugin, but a new contributor has not yet approved the folder. What happens?

options.text: The entries apply only to managed settings, never to a repository
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "the same two keys go in managed settings" for a whole organisation, and the repository's file covers its own contributors.

options.text: The plugin installs at once, because the file is in the repository
options.says: Ruled out because trust comes first: "A repository cannot install code on a machine that has not trusted it."

options.text: Claude Code ignores the entries without a message until trust is given
options.says: The page says the entries "apply only in a folder the contributor has trusted, and in an untrusted folder Claude Code ignores them without a message."

options.text: A prompt appears for each plugin, listing its hooks and its scripts
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "Claude Code ignores them without a message", which describes no prompt.

questions.stem: A subagent should review code and remember wording the team prefers, with that knowledge committed with the code. Which fields fit?

options.text: Read-only tools and the project memory scope
options.says: The page says a reviewer needs `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`, and that the `project` scope is for knowledge that is "shareable via version control".

options.text: Every tool and the user memory scope
options.says: Ruled out because "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", and the `user` scope lives in the home directory and is not committed.

options.text: Read-only tools and the local memory scope
options.says: Ruled out because the `local` scope is for knowledge that "should not be checked in".

options.text: Every tool and no memory field at all
options.says: Ruled out because "Omit it and the subagent inherits every tool", and without `memory` the subagent keeps no knowledge across conversations.
